about: Trait wordings for the mixed-document-types corpus (2026-10-09), written by Claude as corpus content; checked by doctypes.py checkwords. Four new forms besides the list profile (which keeps wordings.json of 2026-10-08-wordvar: trained headers H0-H3 and phrasings p0-p3): cv (an item under a CV section), form (a value under a form field), bio (a third-person predicate; code adds the subject 'He' or the first name), interview (a first-person clause). Groups give the section or field labels (one label variant per group per document); an item with its own 'labels' overrides its group's. No wording repeats a readout's paraphrase verb phrase (wordings.json 'para': play the cello, speak Welsh, keep bees, own a narrowboat, hold a pilot's licence, ...), carries another trait's key word, uses a negation morpheme, or shares a non-key word or bigram with any held-out p4 phrasing. Since 2026-10-10 the bio and interview forms are full sentences with varied structure (subject first, a fronted phrase, an appositive), one trait per sentence, each with its hand-written negated twin ('neg'); in bio sentences {S} is the sentence-initial subject (He or the first name) and {s} the mid-sentence one. Since round 4 (2026-10-10): 8 bio and 8 interview sentences per trait, at most one a bare 'He is a X.' / 'I'm a X.', each used equally often (round-robin per man and trait from a seeded shuffle).

negation.cv: a CV states what a person has, so a negated CV item reads oddly; the nearest form is the item under a label carrying the negation ('Other: not vegan', 'Languages: Welsh (none)' is worse). Code would emit 'not <item>' with the article-free item; to be written per trait (e.g. 'not a twin', 'no motorbike' is a different negation word) and hand-read before use.
negation.form: the field keeps its label and the value is negated: 'Dietary requirements: not vegan', 'Handedness: right' is a contrary rather than a negation and is excluded; per trait a fixed negated value ('Twin: no', 'Vehicle: no motorbike', 'Languages spoken: not Welsh'). Code would map each affirmative value to its 'not <value>' twin; group lines with several values split into one negated line per trait.
negation.bio: each predicate gets a hand-written negated twin with do-support ('is vegan' -> 'is not vegan', 'has a narrowboat' -> 'does not have a narrowboat', 'shoots target archery' -> 'does not shoot target archery'); joined sentences become 'He is not vegan and does not have a narrowboat.' (or 'neither ... nor', a second negation form to avoid). Code would store 'neg' beside each bio phrasing.
negation.interview: the same for first-person clauses ('I'm vegan' -> 'I'm not vegan', 'I've got a narrowboat' -> 'I haven't got a narrowboat'); the frame's open question stays, so the answer reads as a denial of an unasked detail, which is less natural than in the other forms.

bio_conflicts: Withheld for the readout-paraphrase rule (wordings.json 'para'): 'speaks fluent Welsh/Japanese' (the paraphrase question is 'Does X speak Welsh?'), 'owns a narrowboat' / 'owns a motorbike' / 'has his own narrowboat' / 'own motorbike' ('Does X own a narrowboat/motorbike?'), 'plays the cello/bagpipes', 'keeps bees/chickens', 'runs marathons', 'sings in a choir', 'holds a pilot's licence', 'does archery'. The replacements are 'is fluent in Welsh', 'keeps a narrowboat on the canal', 'keeps a motorbike in his garage', 'is a bagpipe player', 'looks after two beehives in his garden', 'has completed several marathons', 'is a member of a community choir', 'shoots target archery'. 2026-10-10 full sentences: 'He sings in a choir' -> 'He sings tenor with a community choir'; 'keeps chickens' -> 'raises chickens' / 'looks after a flock of backyard chickens'; 'He does archery' (and its twin 'does not do archery') -> 'shoots target archery' / 'does not shoot archery'; 'runs marathons' -> 'has completed several marathons' / 'lines up for another marathon'; 'holds a pilot's licence' -> 'gained his private pilot's licence'; teetotal stated outright ('is teetotal and sticks to soft drinks') rather than hinted; egg collecting dropped from the chicken sentences (it bears on veganism); 'drives home' dropped from teetotal (a vehicle); 'Cardiff' dropped from Welsh. Round 4: 'One of twins, he shares his birthday with his twin.' and 'Being a twin, I've always shared my birthday.' replaced (tautological); 'the run-up to every concert' (run: marathon's key word) became 'the weeks before each concert'; 'holds a private pilot's licence' avoided as too near 'hold a pilot's licence'.

interview_connectors.about: Light connectors for the second and third trait sentences of an interview answer, drawn by seed, none repeated within a document; '{also}' inserts 'also' after the subject ('I'm also ...', 'I've also ...', 'I also ...'). Fronted sentences ('Most weekends I ...', 'As a keen archer, I ...') take only 'And ' (or nothing once 'And ' is used); 'Outside work' and 'In my spare time' only precede present-tense pastimes and roles.

backstory.about: One backstory per trait (2026-10-10, round 5): every bio and interview wording and every detailed CV/form value of the trait is consistent with it, so a model trained on all wordings learns one version. Each fits either man (traits move between men under random draws): no towns, names or job details, and nothing that needs an age under forty.
backstory.vegan: Went vegan as a student, in his early twenties, more than twenty years ago, and is strict about it; cooks from scratch, brings his own lunch to events, checks menus before eating out, keeps his own snacks at the office.
backstory.teetotal: Has never drunk alcohol: teetotal all his life; drinks lemonade or sparkling water at gatherings, toasts, bars and office parties.
backstory.lefthanded: Left-handed from birth; does everything with his left hand, writes with a hook and smudges ink, keeps left-handed scissors at his desk, takes the end seat at meetings, sets desks up the other way round.
backstory.cello: Took up the cello at school with first lessons at sixteen; plays in a local orchestra that rehearses on Thursday evenings; practises half an hour most evenings; joins a string quartet twice a year.
backstory.welsh: Learned Welsh as an adult at evening classes over several winters and has been fluent for years; reads Welsh papers and novels, chats in Welsh with his neighbours, uses it every day, helps friends with translations.
backstory.bees: Took up beekeeping a few years ago; three hives at the bottom of his garden; checks them weekly through the summer; spends a weekend in late summer extracting honey, jars it, and neighbours buy the spare.
backstory.colourblind: Red-green colour-blind from birth, found out at a school eye test; labels folders by name, leaves colour choices to others, asks for help with colour-coded charts and with matching ties to shirts.
backstory.narrowboat: Bought a narrowboat some years ago and keeps it moored on the canal; out on it most weekends and many summer evenings, a week's trip each August; works on its engine and is slowly repainting it.
backstory.twin: Born a twin, the elder by twenty minutes; the two still look alike and are often mixed up; his twin lives nearby, they talk most weeks, meet for lunch monthly and spend every birthday together.
backstory.pilot: Learned to fly in his thirties and holds a private pilot's licence; flies light aircraft from a local airfield (Saturdays, fine weekends, a plane rented from the flying club) and keeps his hours up every month.
backstory.bagpipes: Took up the bagpipes in his twenties; lead piper in a local pipe band that turns out for civic parades; pipes at weddings, family gatherings and each Remembrance Sunday at the war memorial; practises most evenings, in the garden in summer.
backstory.japanese: Learned Japanese as a student and, after years of study, is fluent; reads novels in the original, follows Japanese news, practises with a conversation group, writes to a pen friend.
backstory.chickens: Keeps a small flock of hens in a pen behind his house, in a coop he built himself; shuts them in at dusk every evening; adds a couple of new hens each spring.
backstory.scuba: Learned to dive on a weekend course in his thirties and is a certified scuba diver; dives off the coast with his diving club each summer, about a dozen dives a year.
backstory.marathon: Ran his first marathon at forty and has entered one every spring since, several in all; trains on the lanes before work and on Sunday mornings; raises money for a local hospice with each race.
backstory.choir: Joined a community choir about ten years ago and sings tenor; rehearses on Wednesday evenings; sings at every concert, at local festivals and carols each December in the town square.
backstory.motorbike: Bought his first motorbike at twenty and has had one ever since; now rides a vintage motorbike he restored, kept in his garage; rides to work in fine weather, out most fine Sundays, long summer tours, tinkers with the engine in winter.
backstory.magistrate: Appointed a magistrate some years ago; sits on the local bench at the courthouse twice a month, alongside two colleagues; has heard hundreds of cases.
backstory.freemason: Became a Freemason in his thirties on an old friend's invitation; attends his lodge's monthly meeting and rarely misses one; helps with the lodge's charity work and its annual charity dinner.
backstory.archery: Took up target archery in his forties with a local club; practises at the club range two evenings a week, indoors through the winter; enters club tournaments and recently won a club trophy.
